# FAQ-005 Engineering FAQ #5
Revision: Rev A

Question: What lubricant should be used for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01)?
Answer: The lubricant part number for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is CFW-LUB-315. Background: CFW-LUB-315 is the approved lubricant grade for bearings and sliding surfaces on the Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill identified as EQ-P3-L4-RR01. Rationale: Using the specified part ensures compatibility with the metallurgy of the mill components and the environmental conditions in the Heat Treat area. Example application: When replenishing the reservoir or performing a lubrication point fill, confirm the tag on the lubricant container reads CFW-LUB-315 and match the container lot code to the material requisition. Records to keep: Log the container part number, container lot code, date of use, and the technician initials in the lubrication log tied to EQ-P3-L4-RR01. Cross-reference maintenance records to MM-P1-L2-RR01 and SOP-P3-L4-05 for acceptable handling and storage practices.

Question: What mandrel clamp bolt torque is specified for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01)?
Answer: The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01) is 525 N·m. Background: The specified torque value applies to the clamping bolts that secure the mandrel assembly on the Heat Treat mill identified as EQ-P2-L4-RR01. Rationale: Applying the correct torque ensures clamping preload sufficient to maintain mandrel alignment without yielding the bolt or inducing bolt fatigue. Example procedure: During a mandrel change or after a mandrel maintenance event, apply torque to each clamping bolt using a calibrated torque wrench set to 525 N·m and follow the tightening pattern specified in the maintenance manual. Records to keep: Record the torque wrench serial number, calibration date, applied torque value (525 N·m), date, and the technician performing the operation in the bolting maintenance worksheet. Refer to MM-P1-L2-RR01 for the tightening sequence and SOP-P2-L4-03 for bolt handling and inspection steps.

Question: What is the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01)?
Answer: The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is 395 N·m. Background: The clamping system on the Ring Rolling mill EQ-P1-L2-RR01 requires a different torque setting than other mills due to design and bolt grade differences. Rationale: A 395 N·m setting provides the intended clamp force without overstressing the bolt or the mandrel housing, preserving component life and maintaining process stability. Example procedure: Tighten bolts in the specified sequence from the maintenance manual using a calibrated torque tool and verify each bolt reaches 395 N·m. If any bolt does not hold the set torque, follow the inspection steps in SOP-P2-L4-03. Records to keep: Document the torque application event, noting the tool used and calibration traceability, the value applied (395 N·m), and corrective actions if any deviations occurred. Link the entry to MM-P1-L2-RR01 for torque sequence confirmation.

Question: Which lubricant part number is specified for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02)?
Answer: The lubricant part number for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is CFW-LUB-195. Background: CFW-LUB-195 is the approved hydraulic and lubrication fluid for the Heat Treat press EQ-P1-L4-HP02. Rationale: Using the approved part number avoids fluid incompatibility with seals, pumps, and valves and ensures the intended viscosity and additive package are present for safe operation. Example application: When topping up the hydraulic reservoir, verify the container label CFW-LUB-195 and document the lot number and quantity added. If changing fluid supplier or batch, follow the contamination control and flushing steps in SOP-P3-L4-05. Records to keep: Maintain a hydraulic fluid change log that includes the part number CFW-LUB-195, container lot, date, technician initials, and results of any fluid analysis. Reference SOP-P3-L4-05 for fluid handling and MM-P1-L2-RR01 for storage location and segregation.

Question: What is the dust collector alarm setpoint for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03)?
Answer: The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 1240 Pa. Background: The alarm setpoint of 1240 Pa corresponds to the differential pressure across the dust collector filter bank for the shot blast cabinet EQ-P2-L1-SB03. Rationale: The 1240 Pa threshold indicates a filter loading condition requiring filter inspection or change to maintain airflow and capture efficiency without risking damage to the collector or process downtime. Example response: When the instrument indicates the differential pressure has reached 1240 Pa, initiate the filter change and housekeeping procedure outlined in SOP-P2-L4-03. Verify the replacement filters are compatible with the collector and record the before and after differential readings. Records to keep: Log the alarm event with timestamp, measured differential pressure at 1240 Pa, actions taken, replacement filter part numbers, and the technician performing the work. Maintain these entries against the EQ-P2-L1-SB03 equipment record and coordinate with MM-P1-L2-RR01 to schedule follow-up inspections.
